result.rationale: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Zod schemas have no custom toString, so both evaluate to Object.prototype.toString → "[object Object]"; the second key overwrites the first, and zod objects strip unknown keys, so parsed data in sync mode retains only access_token. Expiry from the sync endpoint is discarded, so callers like GoogleCalendarService (`token.expiry_date`) read stale/undefined expiry, causing repeated refreshes. Verified mechanism from the diff.

judged_text: The computed schema keys z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", so the second (optional) key silently overwrites the first and minimumTokenResponseSchema is effectively {access_token: string} — it neither validates the intended numeric expiry field nor retains any extra field. In sync mode every refreshed token response is stripped down to access_token alone: expiry data from the sync endpoint is discarded (callers fall back to stale expiry, causing repeated spurious refreshes), and any contract the sync endpoint was supposed to honor is not actually enforced.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These are evaluated immediately to literal property names (whatever `toString()` returns for those Zod schema objects), not a wildcard/index signature. As a result, the schema does not actually validate “any numeric expiry field” nor “allow other properties”; it will only accept token responses that contain those specific literal keys, and otherwise `safeParse` will fail and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` will throw `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned` in sync mode. The finding’s exact claim about both keys becoming `"[object Object]"` and overwriting down to `{access_token}` isn’t guaranteed from the diff, but the underlying issue (schema is broken and doesn’t enforce the intended contract) is a real defect introduced here.
